category: Total Conflict Deaths — Sahel (2012–2024)
source: Africa Center for Strategic Studies / ACLED cumulative
note: Includes militant Islamist group attacks, inter-communal violence, and security force operations. Africa Center reports 150,000+ deaths from militant groups across the continent; Sahel accounts for the majority.

category: MINUSMA Peacekeepers (2013–2023)
note: 175 deaths by 'malicious act' (hostile fire, IEDs, ambushes); 129 by accident, illness, or other. This makes MINUSMA the deadliest UN peacekeeping mission in history. Personnel from 56 contributing countries.

category: Militants Killed — Operation Serval (2013)
note: French military estimate for jihadist fighters killed during Operation Serval (January–July 2013). Includes airstrikes and ground combat. 7 French soldiers were killed in Serval.

category: Moura Massacre Victims (March 27–31, 2022)
note: UN OHCHR: at least 500 unlawfully executed (min. figure). ~20 women and 7 children killed. 58 women/girls raped. Initial HRW figure ~300. Malian government claims only 203 'terrorists.' The worst single atrocity of the Sahel conflict.

category: Civilian Deaths — Sahel Region (2023)
note: ACLED records 7,800+ civilian deaths in security incidents across the Sahel in the first 8 months of 2023 — a record high. Includes jihadist attacks, inter-communal violence, and security force operations.

category: Conflict Deaths — Burkina Faso (2023)
note: Burkina Faso experienced record violence in 2023, with both jihadist attacks and security force reprisals against civilians. ACLED applies conservative methodology; actual toll likely higher given media restrictions.

category: Ogossagou Massacre — Fulani Civilians (March 23, 2019)
note: Dogon hunters' militia (Dan Nan Ambassagou) attack on Fulani village of Ogossagou, Mopti Region. Worst inter-communal atrocity in Mali's modern history. A second attack on February 14, 2020 killed 35 more.

category: Nondin/Soro Massacre — Civilians (February 25, 2024)
note: Burkina Faso military forces and VDP killed at least 223 civilians including 56 children. Junta denies. HRW and Amnesty call it a potential crime against humanity. No accountability proceedings.

category: JNIM Attack Deaths (2024)
source: Institute for Economics and Peace — GTI 2025
note: 46% increase over 2023. Makes JNIM one of the four deadliest terrorist organizations globally. Average 10 deaths per attack. Operations across Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, and expanding into coastal states.

category: Inates Military Base Attack — Niger (December 10, 2019)
note: Deadliest single attack in Nigerien military history. ISGS pre-dawn motorcycle assault on the Inates military camp, Tillabéri Region.

category: Tongo Tongo Ambush — US/Nigerien Forces (October 4, 2017)
note: Largest US combat loss in Africa since Somalia 1993. ISGS ambush of US Special Forces and Nigerien soldiers near Tongo Tongo village, Tillabéri Region. Prompted congressional investigation.

category: Boulkessi Base Attack — FAMa (June 1, 2025)
note: JNIM assault on Boulkessi military base near Mali-Burkina Faso border. Among the heaviest single-day Malian military losses. Junta has not officially confirmed full casualty figures.

category: Timbuktu Coordinated Attacks — FAMa/Russia (June 2, 2025)
note: JNIM simultaneous assault on Timbuktu military base, checkpoints, and Russian Africa Corps airbase. At least 60 FAMa confirmed killed. Russian casualties not disclosed.

category: French Military Deaths — Operations Serval and Barkhane (2013–2022)
note: 7 killed in Operation Serval (2013–2014), approximately 50 more in Barkhane (2014–2022). France considers these among the highest military casualties in post-WWII French operations.

category: Bagade Military Post Attack — Burkina Faso (March 22, 2026)
source: AFP (via security officials) / NAMPA / TRT Afrika
note: JNIM assault on Bagade military post in northern Burkina Faso killed at least 14 soldiers; some reports indicate up to 20 security force members including VDP killed. JNIM released video showing ~15 dead soldiers. Junta has not issued official casualty confirmation. Part of a sustained JNIM offensive campaign (30+ attacks, 120+ security forces killed) in Burkina Faso since February 2026.

category: Sanama Army Post Attack — Niger (March 25, 2026)
source: Pravda Burkina Faso (citing IS-Sahel claim) / ACLED
note: IS-Sahel claimed responsibility for the attack on Niger Army positions at Sanama, Tillabéri Region. 6 soldiers confirmed killed. Consistent with IS-Sahel's ongoing campaign against military positions in western Niger. Tillabéri has seen nearly 1,300 killed in preceding months per ACLED.

category: Niger — Jihadist Fatalities Post-Coup (2023–2024)
note: Fatalities linked to Islamist militants in Niger quadrupled in the first year after the July 2023 coup, with a 61% increase in battle-related deaths. IS-Sahel and JNIM both escalated operations after US forces were expelled.

category: Niger — Tillabéri Village Massacre (April 18, 2026)
source: Africa Defense Forum / Niger government statement
note: Armed militants killed at least 19 civilians and wounded 2 in a raid on a village in Niger's Tillabéri Region on April 18, 2026. The Niger government described the attackers as 'armed bandits'; the motorcycle-mounted raid pattern is consistent with IS-Sahel Province (ISSP) operations documented extensively across Tillabéri in 2025–2026. Tillabéri has seen over 1,200 conflict deaths in 2025 alone per ACLED. The attack came amid the April 2–17 ISGS-JNIM inter-jihadist clashes in the same region, further complicating the threat environment.

category: ISGS vs. JNIM Inter-Jihadist Clashes — Niger Tillabéri (Apr 2–17, 2026)
note: First documented direct armed combat between IS-Sahel Province (ISGS) and JNIM inside Niger. ISGS initially claimed killing 35 JNIM operatives on April 2; JNIM retaliated April 5. Combined casualties exceeded 50 fighters killed on both sides by April 17. The clashes represent an historic escalation of the inter-jihadist rivalry into Niger territory, where both groups now directly contest the Tillabéri corridor.

category: JNIM Emir Eliminated — Nakamba Sector, Burkina Faso (April 2026)
source: Pravda Burkina Faso / Pravda Mali — April 18, 2026
note: FAB eliminated JNIM field commander Karim Torodo (alias Abdul Bashir), age ~35, who commanded JNIM operations in Burkina Faso's Nakamba sector. Torodo had been wanted since June 2023 with a 175 million CFA franc reward. Operation was part of the FAB's April 2026 counterinsurgency campaign, which also killed approximately 100 militants near Arbinda on April 13–14. JNIM has not issued a martyrdom statement; additional combat casualty figures from the Nakamba operation are unconfirmed.

category: Ayorou NGA Camp Attack — Niger (April 19, 2026)
note: Armed militants attacked a Niger National Guard (Garde Nationale du Niger) camp at Ayorou, Tillabéri Region on April 19, 2026. 3 soldiers confirmed killed. Attack pattern consistent with IS-Sahel Province (ISSP) operations documented in Tillabéri. Niger government did not formally attribute responsibility. Part of sustained ISSP pressure on border security posts along the Mali-Niger corridor following US military withdrawal from Air Base 201 (Agadez) in August 2024.

category: Burkina Faso Civilian Killings — All Parties (Jan 2023–Aug 2025)
source: HRW 'None Can Run Away' Report — April 2, 2026
note: HRW verified 1,837 civilian killings across 57 incidents. Government forces (FAB + VDP militias) attributed with 1,200+ killings; JNIM/IS-Sahel with the remainder. Burkinabè junta denies findings as disinformation. Findings include deliberate JNIM killings of 100+ civilians in Sourou Province (Gonon, Lanfièra, Mara, Tiao villages) accused of VDP support. HRW concluded all parties committed war crimes. No accountability proceedings initiated.

category: JNIM/Katiba Macina — FAMa Airstrike NW Dioura (April 23, 2026)
source: FAMa DIRPA General Staff Statement — April 23, 2026 / Gnawo / Pravda Mali
note: FAMa's General Staff announced airstrikes northwest of Dioura, Mopti Region, neutralized 60+ jihadist fighters and destroyed a major terrorist base. Attribution to JNIM/Katiba Macina is consistent with the operational theater. Figures are self-reported by FAMa; independent verification is impossible due to restrictions on media access to conflict zones in Mopti Region. Dioura area has been a Katiba Macina operational zone since 2016.

category: Mali Crisis — Cumulative Confirmed Casualties (Apr 25–30, 2026)
source: Reuters / Al Jazeera / Wikipedia (2026 Mali attacks) / Long War Journal — April 30, 2026
note: Confirmed deaths: Defence Minister Gen. Sadio Camara (47), his wife, two grandchildren (April 25–26, Kati); plus undisclosed FAMa losses. Goïta's government announced 16 wounded (officially). FAMa and Africa Corps cumulatively claimed 1,000+ insurgents killed and 100+ vehicles destroyed across the April 25–30 period — figures independent analysts describe as grossly inflated given the scale of territorial losses sustained. JNIM and FLA fighter casualties unverifiable. Africa Corps lost 1 Mi-35 helicopter (crew killed). At least 13,000 civilians displaced since October 2025; post-offensive displacement rising. No independent casualty verification possible due to media access restrictions in affected zones.

category: VDP Volunteers Killed — Bagare, Passor Province, Burkina Faso (May 1–2, 2026)
source: The Defense Post / Pravda Burkina Faso — May 2, 2026
note: JNIM motorcycle-mounted assault on VDP post at Bagare, Passor province, northern Burkina Faso. At least 11 VDP (Volunteers for the Defense of the Motherland) volunteers killed in an attack lasting over an hour. Shops, vehicles, and motorcycles burned. JNIM claimed seizure of a 'military post belonging to the Burkinabe militias.' Figures are from NGO/regional media sources; Burkinabè government has not issued an official casualty confirmation. Attack occurred amid simultaneous JNIM pressure on Mali (Bamako siege) demonstrating coordinated multi-country Sahel operations.

category: JNIM + FLA Nationwide Offensive — Mali (April 25–26, 2026)
killed: 4+ confirmed (Camara + family); 'several hundred' militants claimed by FAMa
source: Al Jazeera / Reuters / France 24 / Africanews — April 25–26, 2026
note: Defence Minister General Sadio Camara (age 47) was killed by a JNIM suicide car bomb at his Kati residence on April 25; confirmed April 26. His second wife and two grandchildren were also killed. Government spokesperson confirmed 16 wounded (civilians and military). FAMa claimed 'several hundred assailants neutralized' — not independently verified. No confirmed military death toll released. FLA seized Kidal; Africa Corps withdrew under FLA escort April 26. Kidal losses represent the single largest territorial setback for the Mali-Russia axis since their partnership began.

category: JNIM Assault on Djibo — Burkina Faso (May 11, 2026)
source: NBC News / International Crisis Group / ICTJ — May 2026
note: 100+ confirmed floor per NBC News/ICTJ; ICG cites 'between 100 and 200 civilians and soldiers.' JNIM claimed 200 Burkinabe soldiers killed (unverified). At least 26 civilians summarily executed in neighborhoods. FAB fighter jet turned back; drones not deployed. Largest single JNIM operation in Burkina Faso. Djibo had been blockaded since 2022 with only air resupply; occupation demonstrated JNIM capacity to hold provincial capitals for operational periods.

category: JNIM Attack on Porga Military Post — Benin (May 7, 2026)
note: JNIM attacked a Beninese military post at Porga, Atacora Department, northern Benin. 7 soldiers killed; weapons and motorcycles seized. Represents JNIM's southward expansion into Gulf of Guinea coastal states through the W-Arly-Pendjari park corridor. Confirmed by pro-junta/ACLED-aligned monitoring; Beninese government has not issued an official statement as of May 12, 2026.

category: JNIM Assault on Diapaga — Est Region, Burkina Faso (May 12–13, 2026)
note: Zagazola Makama reported 50+ soldiers and VDP volunteers killed as JNIM overran the Diapaga army outpost in Burkina Faso's Est Region. JNIM combined the Djibo (May 11) and Diapaga (May 13) attacks in a 200+ total claim; Diapaga-specific figures cannot be independently disaggregated. FAB has not issued official figures. Diapaga was the last major FAB buffer before the Togolese border; its fall represents JNIM's southernmost confirmed provincial-outpost seizure in Burkina Faso's Est Region.

category: Fulani Civilian Executions — Diafarabé, Mopti Region, Mali (May 12–15, 2026)
source: Amnesty International / FIDH / The Africa Report — May 15, 2026
note: At least 30 Fulani men arrested May 12 at Diafarabé cattle market by Malian soldiers and Dozo militia; 22 bodies found May 15 in two mass graves on south bank of Niger River. Victims aged 32–67; bound, blindfolded, transported by canoe, throats slit. 8 arrested men unaccounted for. Malian junta has not issued a statement. Amnesty International called for 'urgent investigation.' Pattern consistent with Moura (2022, 500+ killed) and Ogossagou (2019, ~160 killed) — FAMa/auxiliary killings of Fulani men presumed to be JNIM sympathizers based on ethnicity. The Africa Report quoted survivor: 'They slit their throats one by one.'

category: JNIM Twin Village Massacres — Korikori and Gomossogou, Mopti Region (May 8, 2026)
source: Al Jazeera / AFP / Gulf News / WAMAPS — May 7–8, 2026
note: AFP initially reported 'at least 30 killed'; diplomatic sources told Reuters the toll reached at least 50; WAMAPS cited 'more than 50 villagers killed, several still missing.' JNIM simultaneously raided Korikori and Gomossogou in Mopti Region, central Mali, on the night of May 6–7. Victims included militiamen, teenagers, and children. JNIM cited the Dan Na Ambassagou (DNA) self-defense militia's cooperation with FAMa as justification. FAMa launched a subsequent 'targeted operation' neutralizing approximately a dozen JNIM fighters. No independent verification of exact toll possible under junta media restrictions in Mopti Region.

category: MSF-Documented Atrocities — Malian Refugees in Mauritania (May 2026)
killed: Undetermined (mass atrocity testimonies; no systematic count)
note: MSF coordinator Mayoury Savant confirmed staff at Doueinkara healthcare centre, Hodh Chargui region, Mauritania are documenting systematic torture, sexual violence against women and men, being burned alive and beheaded, massacres, looting, and destruction of livelihoods among ~300,000 Malian refugees. AFP: 'The survivors' accounts depict a level of horror rarely seen on such a scale in the region.' Alleged perpetrators: FAMa and Africa Corps (formerly Wagner). FIDH/TRIAL International/PALU filed a landmark case before the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights on April 20, 2026 — the first against a state for contracting private military actors. Malian junta has not responded to the MSF disclosures; media embargo prevents independent access to northern Mali conflict zones.

category: JNIM Goubré IDP Camp Massacre — Centre-Nord, Burkina Faso (May 22, 2026)
killed: 80 total (72 civilians: 45 men, 23 women, 2 girls, 2 boys + 8 VDP fighters)
source: HRW documentation / UN OCHA statement / JNIM claim — May 22–24, 2026
note: JNIM attacked the Goubré internally displaced persons camp in Burkina Faso's Centre-Nord Region on May 22, 2026. HRW documented 80 killed including 72 civilians across demographic groups: 45 men, 23 women, 2 girls, and 2 boys. Approximately 40 injured. The camp housed ~3,500 displaced people who had already fled earlier JNIM violence. JNIM claimed on May 24 that the attack targeted VDP (Volunteers for the Defense of the Motherland) fighters who used the camp. UN Humanitarian Coordinator Alain Akpadji formally condemned the attack on May 24 and confirmed an aid worker was killed. The camp was shut down following the massacre, forcing 3,500 survivors to seek refuge again. Burkinabè junta has not issued an official casualty confirmation; access to Centre-Nord remains restricted. One of the most severe single JNIM atrocities against internally displaced civilians in the 14-year Sahel crisis.

category: FAMa Drone Strike on Civilians — Tene, San District, Ségou Region, Mali (May 18, 2026)
note: FAMa armed drones struck a motorbike procession of villagers in Tene locality, San District, Ségou Region, central Mali on May 18, 2026. At least 10 civilians confirmed killed, including children. AFP wire: a local resident stated '10 of our children' were killed; a security source acknowledged drones targeted 'a procession of motorbikes following one another' that drew military attention. A survivor: 'What was supposed to be a moment of joy in the village turned into immense sorrow.' Malian junta has not issued a statement. The strike adds to an acute civilian harm convergence in May 2026: Diafarabé mass graves (22 Fulani men executed, May 12–15), JNIM's Korikori-Gomossogou massacres (May 8, 30–50+ killed), and OHCHR's 'gravely concerning' alert (May 5–6).

category: Civilians Killed — Titao-Sollé Convoy Attack, Loroum Province, Burkina Faso (May 29, 2026)
source: Ghana Peace Journal Sahel Diaries / Wikipedia: Titao ambush — May 29, 2026
note: JNIM militants on motorcycles attacked a trading convoy on the Titao-Sollé axis in Loroum Province, Nord Region, Burkina Faso, killing at least 15 civilians including women and children. Burkinabè junta did not issue official figures. Consistent with JNIM's sustained pressure on northern BF commercial supply routes. Part of the ongoing May 2026 multi-district JNIM campaign across Burkina Faso.

category: ICRC Aid Convoy Ambush — Barsalogho, Sanmatenga Province, Burkina Faso (May 29–30, 2026)
source: Wikipedia: Barsalogho aid convoy attack / Ghana Peace Journal — May 2026
note: JNIM ambushed an ICRC-affiliated aid convoy returning from Foube refugee camp near Barsalogho, escorted by gendarmes. Initial toll: 5 gendarmes + 5 civilians killed; final toll: 13 killed. 40 wounded; 6 gendarmes missing. Among the dead: an ICRC ambulance driver and nurse — persons protected under the Red Cross emblem under IHL. The first confirmed killing of ICRC-emblem personnel in the 2026 Burkina Faso conflict. Junta has not confirmed figures.

category: Burkina Faso JNIM Atrocities — May 2026 (All Confirmed Incidents)
source: NBC News / HRW / TRT World / Ghana Peace Journal / Zagazola Makama / Wikipedia — May 2026
note: Five confirmed JNIM-attributed major atrocities in Burkina Faso in May 2026: (1) Bagare VDP post, Passor Province (May 1–2, 11+ VDP killed); (2) Djibo military base/city occupation, Sahel Region (May 11, 100–200 killed — soldiers, VDP, civilians); (3) Diapaga army outpost, Est Region (May 12–13, 50+ killed); (4) Goubré IDP camp, Centre-Nord Region (May 22, 80 killed including 72 civilians — 45 men, 23 women, 4 children); (5) Kompienbiga livestock market, Est Region (May 31, ~30 killed). Plus JNIM's ICRC convoy ambush near Barsalogho (May 29–30, 13 killed including ICRC humanitarian workers; 40 wounded) and the Titao-Sollé trading convoy massacre (May 29, 15+ civilians killed). Cumulative floor estimate: approximately 300+ killed in verified JNIM operations in Burkina Faso during May 2026 alone — the deadliest single month in Burkina Faso's insurgency history. Traoré junta has not issued official aggregate figures. Independent access to conflict zones remains severely restricted.

category: Civilian Massacre — Kompienbiga Livestock Market, Est Region, Burkina Faso (May 31, 2026)
note: Armed gunmen on motorcycles attacked the livestock market in Kompienbiga (Kompienga Province, Est Region) on May 31, 2026, killing approximately 30 civilians before fleeing. Security source attributed the attack to 'armed groups with links to al-Qaeda and Daesh.' Attack occurred during Eid al-Adha (Day 2), when livestock markets are the principal commercial gathering points. Kompienbiga is 60 km south of Diapaga — seized by JNIM on May 13, 2026. Traoré junta did not issue official figures. Brings the total confirmed JNIM-attributed major atrocity deaths in Burkina Faso in May 2026 to approximately 300+ across five distinct incidents.

category: Civilian Casualties — JNIM Landmine, Bamako–Kayes Highway (June 1, 2026)
note: Passenger bus struck a landmine on the Bamako–Kayes highway on June 1, 2026, killing 8 civilians and injuring 42. The western supply corridor connecting Bamako to Senegal and Mauritania. Attack came during the post-Eid 'easing' window identified by The Africa Report — demonstrating JNIM's continued operational tempo on supply corridors even outside declared escalation periods. Consistent with JNIM's 'strategy of asphyxiation' targeting the Dakar–Bamako trade corridor documented by ISS Africa (June 4, 2026).

category: FAB/VDP Killed — Koumbri Military Base, Yatenga Province, Burkina Faso (June 1, 2026)
source: Crisis Group CrisisWatch / Islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso — June 2026
note: JNIM fighters overran the military base at Koumbri (Yatenga Province, Nord Region, Burkina Faso) on June 1, 2026, reportedly killing 45 Burkinabè soldiers and 10 VDP — one of the deadliest single-day FAB tolls of the conflict if confirmed. Source: Crisis Group CrisisWatch aggregate and Wikipedia insurgency timeline — no specific primary source article confirmed. Traoré junta imposes strict information blackout on all security incidents; independent verification is not possible. Figures should be treated as preliminary pending independent confirmation. The attack would represent the sixth major JNIM operation in Burkina Faso since May 1, building on the record May 2026 campaign (~300+ killed).

category: FAB/VDP Killed — Di Military Camp & Dalan/Tiéré, Sourou Province, Burkina Faso (Jul 4, 2026)
source: AFP via The Defense Post / allAfrica — Jul 7–8, 2026
note: Coordinated JNIM assault on the Di military camp (Sourou Province) plus simultaneous strikes on Dalan and Tiéré localities and border positions at Gorgadji, Thiou, and Diin. AFP-sourced reporting cited ~14 soldiers plus 7 civilian VDP killed at Di alone; combined toll across the weekend's attacks ranged from 'at least 22 soldiers and militia' (The Defense Post) to 'at least fifty soldiers and VDP' (allAfrica/RFI relay). JNIM claimed responsibility; camps were reportedly looted of weapons.

category: Civilian Casualties — Africa Corps Su-24 Airstrike, Kyrnia, Mopti Region (Jun 15, 2026)
note: HRW investigation (19 interviews, satellite imagery, video analysis) found an Africa Corps Su-24 dropped two munitions on Kyrnia village on a market day: first strike near the village chief's residence killed his wife and two children plus one more child; second strike ~20m away on a cattle market killed four men, including three merchants. ~100 JNIM fighters were present but concentrated ~150m from the impact sites, with no evidence of a military objective at the points actually struck. HRW called on Mali's junta to independently investigate, saying authorities 'cannot hide behind laws-of-war violations committed by their Russian allies.'

category: FAN Killed — Bankilaré–Téra Ambush, Tillabéri Region, Niger (Jul 17, 2026)
source: Niger Ministry of Defence / RFI (via Pravda Niger relay) — Jul 17–20, 2026
note: Niger Armed Forces liaison detachment ambushed near Doungouro village on contested ISSP/JNIM ground. Official government figure (16 killed) diverges nearly 3x from RFI's unofficial reporting (47+ killed including the unit commander) — a gap consistent with a pattern of official undercounting. African Union Commission condemned the attack Jul 18.

category: FAN/National Guard Killed — Dankassari & N'Guigmi Base Attacks, Niger (Jul 31, 2026)
source: Zagazola Makama / Arab News (AFP) / The Whistler — Aug 1, 2026
note: Suspected ISSP fighters overran a forward operating base at Dankassari (Dosso Region, 21 killed) and attacked a National Guard post at N'Guigmi (Diffa Region, 14–17 killed depending on source, with figures disputed across outlets citing the same underlying reporting chain). Group attribution is also disputed: Niger's state news agency attributed the attacks loosely to 'Boko Haram,' while security-analyst sourcing frames them under ISSP/Islamic State Sahel Province. No full official government confirmation of the combined total.

category: FAMa Killed — JNIM Assault on San Barracks, Ségou Region, Mali (Aug 9, 2026)
source: AFP via NAMPA / Club of Mozambique — Aug 9, 2026
note: JNIM fighters attacked and temporarily occupied FAMa's main barracks in San, killing at least 10 soldiers and seizing military equipment. Mali's military said it conducted a 'vigorous riposte,' claiming ~40 militants killed — unverified. San is well south of the historical northern front line, illustrating JNIM's continued southward operational reach toward Bamako's approaches.

category: Sahel-wide Militant Islamist Violence Deaths (12mo to mid-2026)
note: 42% of Africa's continental total (23,872) for the 12 months to mid-2026 — deadliest region on the continent for a fourth consecutive year. JNIM ~76% of regional deaths, ISGS/IS-Sahel ~19%. Africa Center cautions the true toll is likely undercounted given reporting restrictions imposed by the military juntas in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.

category: Africa Corps Massacre — Bombori Village, Mopti Region, Mali (July 10, 2026)
note: HRW documented (remote interviews Jul 19-30) that 100+ Russian Africa Corps fighters, accompanied by 4 Malian soldiers as interpreters, raided the Fulani neighborhood of Bombori on Jul 10 at ~5 a.m. Six civilians shot while fleeing; three more detained and executed (one beheaded). At least 80 men and boys rounded up and beaten. 8 homes and 5 granaries burned; only the Fulani neighborhood was targeted, not the neighboring Rimaibe area. JNIM has controlled Bombori since 2017 with a base ~1km away but had departed the night before. HRW letters to Russian and Malian defense ministries (Aug 4-5) went unanswered. HRW: the Malian junta appears to have given Africa Corps a green light to kill civilians.
